current_episode.title: Building Community: The Impact of Leadership in the Construction Industry with Marcus Vega

guest.bio_context: Marcus Vega has been in the construction industry for close to 35 years, starting with basement waterproofing, progressing to drywall and framing after joining the carpenters union. He was hired by Alexander, Boots Family Companies slightly over a year ago as a General Foreman after networking at the KCA celebration in 2025, where he met Jeff Smith. He won the 2026 KCA Labor Champion award, officially named the Thomas George Memorial Community Service Award, for his work mentoring apprentices and supporting young people in the trades.

context.real_quote: I want to be a better person tomorrow than I am today, and each and every day I want to exemplify that at the job.

pending_qa.q: What is the significance of the Thomas George Memorial Community Service Award that Marcus Vega won?
pending_qa.r: The award was created close to 10 years ago by the KCA board to recognize labor champions in the construction industry, named after Thomas George, the executive director of the KCA in the seventies and eighties who was a best friend to labor leaders. Marcus was the first recipient in the award's 10-year history to be nominated by two different KCA employers—a previous employer and his current employer.

pending_qa.q: What are Marcus Vega's leadership principles and career aspirations?
pending_qa.r: Marcus aspires to become a superintendent and believes in being a fair but firm leader, similar to boxing referee Joe Cortez. He maintains respect by referring to people as Mr. and Miss, says thank you, and greets people with good morning, believing these simple gestures help get more out of people. He does not want his position to change his character and commits to being a good role model rather than becoming distant or rude like some construction management personnel.

pending_qa.q: How did Marcus Vega's first employer impact his career?
pending_qa.r: When hired by Mr. Strawbridge at Strawbridge Enterprises, Marcus received a complete starter set of tools including a tool bag, T-square, utility knife, and meat saw. Strawbridge gave Marcus the tools as a gift after recognizing his work ethic and potential, telling him he would be the one person to make a career out of it. Marcus still has some of those original tools, including the T-square and utility knife.
